findings.title: Decode is memory-bound until batch ~257
findings.body: On H100, Llama-3.1-8B's FFN GEMMs cross the roofline ridge at batch 257 in BF16 and at the same batch in FP8, because FP8 halves weight bytes and doubles peak FLOPs, so the ridge moves with it. Below that, each extra user costs almost nothing per step.

findings.title: 25% of 70B single-user decode on 8x H100 is fixed cost
findings.body: Kernel launches (18%) and 160 latency-bound all-reduces (7%) per token do not shrink with TP, so splitting further stops paying off before weight streaming does.

findings.title: LPU: 6.6x faster per user, 12x less throughput per chip
findings.body: Llama-3.1-70B: the fastest GPU layout reaches 215 tok/s per user; 197 Groq 3 LPUs reach 1424 (modeled, assumed compute). At a 50 tok/s/user SLA the best layout is 2x NVIDIA B200 (HGX, 180GB) TP2 PP1 fp8 at 1609 tok/s per device.

findings.title: MLA caches 7.3x less KV per token
findings.body: DeepSeek-V3 stores a 576-dim latent per layer (34 KiB/token in FP8) vs Llama-3.1-405B's GQA K/V (252 KiB/token), so far more users fit per GPU.

findings.title: Weights alone need 157 Groq 3 LPUs for 70B
findings.body: SRAM-only chips must hold every weight on chip; KV cache needs more chips on top. That is why NVIDIA pairs LPUs with HBM GPUs instead of replacing them.
